blocks.text: A prompt is the message you send to the AI. The clearer your prompt, the better the answer. The AI knows nothing about you except what you write.
The four ingredients of a good prompt

items: Task – what exactly you want (write, explain, compare, list).
Context – who it's for and why ("for my boss", "I'm a beginner", "I have 30 minutes").
Details or an example – what you already have, what you like and don't like.
Format – how you want the answer (5 bullet points, a table, short, under 100 words).

blocks.text: Strong: "Write a short, cheerful Instagram post for my bakery, which turns 5 this Saturday. Mention 20% off croissants. Max 3 sentences and 3 hashtags."
If the answer isn't good, don't start over – say what to change: "shorter", "more formal", "add an example".
You can start with "Act as an experienced coach" or "You are a maths teacher". This helps the AI hit the right tone and level.
You are an experienced personal trainer. Make me a home workout plan for 3 days a week, 20 minutes each, no equipment. I'm a complete beginner. Give the answer as a table.
With Claude, feel free to write longer, more detailed prompts – it follows long instructions well. You can also paste a whole text and ask it to work with it.
In ChatGPT you can save lasting instructions about yourself in the settings (for example "answer briefly"), so you don't have to repeat them every time.
Gemini can use Google Search, so you can ask for up-to-date information in your prompt – but always check the sources it gives.
